English: Gem Locker
A sturdy wooden chest with iron bands, hidden in a guarded storeroom, used to secure precious stones and minor valuables.
Coin Room
A rough chamber for storing basic coin reserves, often little more than a locked chest behind a guard.
Stone Vault
A secure, stone-lined chamber with a reinforced door, protecting greater wealth and serving as a symbol of growing prosperity.
Guarded Treasury
A reinforced treasury chamber with armed guards and basic traps, deterring thieves and boosting the lords authority.
Treasure Gallery
A vaulted room displaying the lords wealth, with guards, iron doors, and displays for coin and jewels, impressing guests and vassals alike.
Gold Chamber
An opulent, multi-layered vault of brick and iron, watched day and night, its gold reserves supporting armies and acts of diplomacy.
Royal Treasury
A vast, heavily guarded suite of vaults holding the crowns reserves, with complex locks, alarm devices, and a treasury administrator.
Jewel House
A secure annex dedicated to the storage and display of royal gems, regalia, and rare artifacts, guarded by elite retainers.
Imperial Treasury
The heart of royal finances, with multiple vaults, secret passages, and a permanent staff, symbolizing the might of the realm.
Palace Treasure Hall
A grand, marble-lined hall at the palaces heart, showcasing the realms immense riches
French: its security is unmatched, and its splendor inspires awe.
